title: What is known about 1RB0LF_0LC0RE_0RA1LD_1LB0LD_0RA1RC_1LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LF_0LC0RE_0RA1LD_1LB0LD_0RA1RC_1LA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. At each left record the tape is 0^inf ell B>c (10)^D1 x1 (10)^D2 x2 … with single cells x = 1 or 0. The blocks form a binary counter, incremented once per long sweep while the first block counts down by 2. An exact block macro machine (py/blockmm.py) maps each record to the next by cached symbolic crossings; it agrees with direct simulation at all 15,144 records of the first 3·108 steps. Its 387 crossing rules used in the first 300,000 records are proved in Lean (kernel) for every block size and tape, and so is the even long sweep over any list of blocks (carry_even). The composition of rules is trusted Python, not Lean. The macro run: no halt through 16,409,053 left records and 338,536,834,271,065 steps (3.39·1014), across 28 resets. At the resets the countdown block follows X → 3X/2 + 1 (X even) or (3X + 5)/2 (X odd), heuristically, so the long run is a Collatz-like question; random block lists that look like records can halt, so no simple invariant is available.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: The short sweep
claims.text: B>0 (10)^(2x+4) 1 0 0 0 R becomes B>0 (10)^(2x+4) 1 1 0 1 1 0 R at the next left record, in 12x + 36 steps, for every x and every tape R (short, from short_raw by bbtools.symtm.prove).

claims.title: The run reaches it
claims.text: From blank tape the machine is at B>0 (10)^12 1 0 0 0 … after 2,438 steps (reach2438, list simulator evaluated by the kernel), and by short at the next left record after 2,522 (reach2522).

claims.title: The crossing rules of the macro machine
claims.text: All 387 crossing rules that the block macro machine uses in its first 300,000 left records (111 moving right, 276 moving left), each steps n start = some end for every value of the block parameter t and every tape outside the known context, by bbtools.symtm.prove.

claims.title: The even long sweep
claims.text: 0^inf B>0 (1010)^(a+2) 1 10 1 [(1010)^(t+4) 1]^ts 10 (1010)^(b+4) 0 R reaches 0^inf B>0 1 0 1 (0101)^a 0 1 0 0 0 1 0 1 0 1 [(0101)^(t+3) 0 1 0 0 1]^ts 0 1 0 1 (0101)^(b+3) 0 1 1 0 R for all a, b, every list ts and every R: one increment of the counter, carried through any number of even 1-blocks.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 55,183 cells have been visited and 27,582 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The macro machine is exact
claims.text: py/check_macro.py runs the macro machine from the first record and compares step count, head cell and blocks with the direct simulator c/recp.c at every left record: all 15,144 records up to step 299,979,488 agree. It also gives record 300,000 at step 116,666,829,938, as the earlier direct run c/rec18.c did.

claims.title: No halt in 3.39·10<sup>14</sup> steps
claims.text: py/run_macro.py: no halt through 16,409,053 left records, 338,536,834,271,065 steps, and 28 resets. The bookkeeping that glues crossings together (word stacks, normalize, reparse) is Python, not Lean; the rules applied in the first 300,000 records are the Lean ones.

claims.title: No halt in 1.17·10<sup>11</sup> steps (direct)
claims.text: c/rec18.c, direct simulation with a 128-bit step count: no halt in the first 116,666,829,938 steps, through 300,000 left records.

claims.title: The reset map
claims.text: At each of the 28 resets found, the countdown block X becomes X' = 3X/2 + 1 (X even) or (3X + 5)/2 (X odd) at the next one: 142, 214, 322, 484, 727, 1093, …, 8,204,530. The next block follows Y' ≈ 3Y/2 + c with c slowly growing (8 to 40). Each phase takes about 2.25 times as many steps as the last.

claims.title: Shape of the records
claims.text: In the first 105 records: no block (0, 1) after the first; after a 0-block the next block has D + x even; the first block has D + x odd (or, right after a reset, 1 B>1 then (0, 0) then a block with D + x odd). 99.99% of macro steps are a single sweep: crossings right, one turn, crossings left.

claims.title: These patterns are not an invariant
claims.text: py/random_check.py: one macro step from 20,000 random block lists. 2 of the 14,742 lists that obey the record patterns halt (and 2 of the 5,258 that do not), so the patterns alone do not exclude the halt.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Missing: a Lean proof that the composition of the macro rules is sound, and an invariant of the reachable block lists that excludes 1 A>1, or a halts_iff reduction to the Collatz-like reset map.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. The tape is a binary counter on blocks of 10s, each closed by one cell. Every sweep adds one while a countdown block shrinks; when it runs out, the blocks come back about 3/2 larger, by a Collatz-like rule. An exact macro machine, its rules proved in Lean, finds no halt in 3.39·1014 steps.

facts.text: Every crossing rule of the macro machine used in 300,000 records, for all block sizes.
No halt in the macro run, which matches direct simulation record for record.
The reset map, seen at all 28 resets.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.495). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 55,183 cells (40,157 left of the start, 13 right), with a density of 1s of 0.5.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Blocks at a left record
html: Look at the tape when state B stands left of every cell visited so far. Write P for the pair 10. The tape is 0^inf ell B>c P^D1 x1 P^D2 x2 …: runs of P, each closed by a single cell i (a 1) or o (a 0). The blank right end counts as endless blocks P^0 o. Right after a reset, B carries an extra 1 on its left.

sections.heading: One sweep, one increment
html: From the record the head runs right with a phase bit: state A (α) or B/E (β). Crossing a block P^D x flips the phase when D + x is even, and the sweep turns at the first o-block with D + phase odd. On the way out 1010 is rewritten as 1100; the way back restores it. The result is one increment of a binary counter: the first block loses 2, the even i-blocks before the turn become o-blocks, the turning o-block becomes an i-block. Lean proves this for any list of blocks (carry_even), and the short sweep that follows (short).

sections.heading: An exact block macro machine
html: py/blockmm.py keeps the tape as two stacks of words, each a block written as (1010)^(t+4) x or 10 (1010)^(t+4) x (or literally when short). Crossing a word of a given kind from a given situation is computed once by a symbolic run valid for every t, and cached. 387 such rules cover the first 300,000 records, and each is a Lean theorem. The glue between them is Python: it is checked against direct simulation at 15,144 records, not proved.

sections.heading: A Collatz-like reset map
html: When the countdown runs out, the next block X becomes the countdown. At every reset so far X goes to 3X/2 + 1 (X even) or (3X + 5)/2 (X odd), and each phase is about 2.25 times as long as the last. Some of the resets (X, Y the first two blocks after it):

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The only halting transition is F reading 1, and F is entered only from A reading 1. So the machine halts exactly on 1 A>1. The run never produces it. But random block lists that share every visible pattern of the records halt now and then (2 in 14,742), so ruling out the halt needs a finer description of which lists the run reaches.

sections.heading: What is proved
html: Lean, kernel: the 387 crossing rules (lean/Rules.lean), the even long sweep over any block list (lean/Sweep.lean), the short sweep and the reach from blank tape.
Computed: the macro machine matches direct simulation at 15,144 records; the macro run finds no halt in 3.39·1014 steps.
Open: Lean soundness of composing the rules, an invariant excluding the halt, and so the question.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

family: binary counter on (10)^D x blocks with a countdown block; Collatz-like 3/2 reset map
summary: A binary counter on blocks (10)<sup>D</sup> x with a countdown block; an exact block macro machine (387 crossing rules, all kernel-proved in Lean for every block size) runs it with no halt in 3.39·10<sup>14</sup> steps. The resets follow a Collatz-like 3/2 map; no invariant excluding the halt is known.
